backbone: Recover quasi-divisorial valuations from alternating pairs, then curves, true divisors and rational subfields, then the field from simultaneous values; uniqueness up to scalar and Frobenius.
quote: The groups $`K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell`$ and $`K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell`$, together with their full bilinear product, determine the perfect closure and its constant field.

backbone: Lower-bound sieve survivors via a decreasing-prime (Buchstab) tree evaluated at the linear-sieve limit, controlling discrepancies by an inverse estimate, variance bounds and stopped counts.
quote: Our proof also reaches this limiting parameter. It keeps a boundary contribution that disappears from the leading linear-sieve term, and then controls the discrepancy between this reference calculation and the actual prescribed classes.

backbone: Reduce via the relative Iitaka fibration and an exact canonical-bundle-type comparison to (W,T,M), then apply an adjoint-addition principle fed by Hodge-line positivity and log-general-type addition.
quote: Section~\ref{application:section} then returns once to the original fibration, applies the addition principle to $(W,T,M)$, and derives the ordinary, logarithmic, characteristic-zero, and core consequences.

backbone: Build an arithmetic ball-quotient arrangement with a distinguished abelian surface, show infinite cyclic pi_1 image via hyperbolic path graphs, then realize projectively as a fourfold.
quote: We construct a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover is not Stein.

backbone: Construct the intrinsic quotient of the semialgebraic cover, prove its deck action discrete with bounded-symmetric base (scaling/peak-function argument), split off compact fibres and affine factor, assemble the product.
quote: In the present proof, the intrinsic quotient is constructed before its deck action is proved discrete and its base is identified as symmetric.

backbone: Assume excess integral-means growth; build an affine-invariant probability law on conformal maps from a transfer operator eigenmeasure; a saddle-maximum pairing forces the opposite Jacobian sign.
quote: Our proof encodes hypothetical excess growth in a probability law on conformal maps. That law imposes an algebraic sign on an expected Jacobian; a geometric pairing of critical points imposes the opposite sign.

backbone: Probabilistic method: a random periodic set built by tree routing over separated index windows hits every normalized scaled progression with high probability; summable dilated unions give the avoiding compact set.

backbone: Extract from the permanent (coefficient-selecting projection, char-2 adjugate scheme, characteristic transfer) a smooth form with (r-1)(d-1) of order m^3, then bound bdc of smooth forms by counting simple polar intersections.
quote: Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth-border} proves the version needed here, including persistence of finitely many simple polar intersections in one sufficiently close determinant under an arbitrary coefficientwise approximation.

backbone: Explicit randomized algorithm: phased matching states with priced logarithmic steps, a recursive routing sparsifier and frozen forest decompositions, analysed for almost-linear cost and correctness with probability 2/3.
quote: We prove that maximum-cardinality matching in a simple undirected graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges can be found by one uniform randomized algorithm in $(n+m)^{1+o(1)}$ time.

backbone: Reduce a padded diagonal language (hard at every length by hierarchy) through a circuit-simulating arc-consistency instance compressed into explicit graph pairs whose bijective-game equivalence matches consistency.
quote: Duplicator wins the $K$-pair bijective game on $G^0,G^1$ if and only if the instance has individual-edge arc consistency.

backbone: Assume a least failing order; reduce to a zero-entropy finite-alphabet witness, analyse its limit joining via saturated ordered arrays and a unitary label group, and show positive entropy, a contradiction.
quote: Suppose an invertible mixing transformation fails to be mixing of every order.

backbone: Sample a graph from a finite probability space with a triangle-free F2-tensor hole relation; a supersaturation theorem (entropy, moments, energy increment) forces conflicts so no large clique minor survives.
quote: For finite sampling we adapt the deterministic fingerprint procedure of Kleitman and Winston

backbone: Random ordered incident-flag graph in PG(d,q) is K_{d+1}-free; a compression/entropy argument (assume large independent sets, describe them too briefly) shows small independence number with positive probability; upper bound classical.
quote: A position receives a random incident pair \((a,b)\), where \(a\) is a point of \(\PG(4,q)\) and \(b\) is a hyperplane containing it.

backbone: Build reflection-positive tuple laws giving a signed multilinear form dominating a density power; Fourier/circle-method comparison shows the form contracts on passing to shorter progressions; iterate (power-saving induction).
quote: The square-difference method constructs a multilinear form which dominates a fixed power of density, and proves that this form contracts on passing to shorter intervals.

backbone: Reduce via Cohen factorization to a finite free complex; bound it using an additive normalized length built separately in characteristic p, mixed, and (by specialization) zero.
quote: The complex $F$ has length at most $h$, has $F_0=T$, and is contractible away from the closed point. Its differentials have entries in $\mathfrak t$, and its ranks have alternating sum zero.

backbone: Build an explicit finite lattice carrying all normal-subgroup tests; a representation would give subgroup intervals with arbitrarily long tested chains, excluded via classification-based growth and rank bounds.
quote: We also construct a nonrepresentable family directly.

backbone: Renormalization: an exact change-of-scale map with contracting irrelevant coordinates and one expanding thermal direction; a stable graph/shooting selects criticality, then observables are compared with pure Ising.
quote: Sections~\ref{sec:variance} and~\ref{sec:trajectory} establish the variance recursion and tune a trajectory with decaying disorder.

backbone: Upper bound: multiscale greedy covers charged to one sausage measure via uniform stopped-Green-density tails. Lower bound: a weak-limit mass with gauge ball bounds on every segment.
quote: Here a greedy family of disjoint disks is charged to one finite-mesh sausage measure, and the quantitative ribbon probability specifies the logarithmic gauge.

backbone: Construct single-fold polynomial systems: unique codes from a rank-one elliptic curve give a uniquely represented intermediate-growth function, hence a single-fold power graph, then a unique encoding of a halting run.
quote: We first obtain unique arithmetic witnesses, then a unique encoding of the accepting run.

backbone: Reduce to contractibility of the spherical-coset poset; a fusion-labelled categorical Artin action gives a well-ordered harmonic height, and the poset is contracted sublevel by sublevel using local rigidity estimates.
quote: Our proof uses the classical spherical-coset reduction and contracts that poset directly for every finite-rank matrix.

backbone: Three standard bases give the lower bound; upper bound: a certified exhaustive seed-ball cover of second bases plus local exclusion of two further bases, run under a binary64 contract.
quote: The upper bound is computer-assisted: under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions, a complete execution of the documented verification pipeline excludes four arbitrary complex bases.

backbone: Exhibit a weakly coupled two-centre three-electron molecule with explicit charge; median-plane density asymptotics plus an ensemble kinetic certificate force any representing potential into a weighted-trace contradiction.
quote: We construct a finite three-electron Coulomb molecule whose spin-summed ground-state density cannot be reproduced by any ground-state ensemble of noninteracting electrons in a single real, spin-independent local potential

backbone: Assume failure (self-bicentralizing counterexample); left/right multiplication isometries satisfy R=L exp(iX tensor Y), and uniform modular-energy estimates with repeated tensor tests contradict; pass to the core for general inclusions.

backbone: Known upper bound; for the lower bound assume a cover rate above 2rc, convert comparison to a bundle embedding, apply MU-based compression to lower covering order: contradiction.

backbone: Upper bound via cyclic chains; lower bound: a rational character estimate (maximizing pro-p tower, integration congruences) glued across heights, then at a least failing height a support splitting contradicts irreducibility.
quote: At a least height where the proposed bound fails, the estimates isolate the offending subgroup component from the other components.

backbone: Prove uniform Walsh-norm decay for finite-rank operators (iterated halving), transfer it via AP to a compact factorization of the identity, excluding uniform l_1^n copies.
quote: Uniform Walsh decay passes to \(J\), and then to every finite Walsh input in \(X\). Uniform copies of \(\ell_1^s\) would contradict that decay.

backbone: Run a localized Kahler-Ricci flow, control it by disc-envelope and Harnack inequalities to get shrinking holomorphic charts, then assemble them by complex dynamics into a biholomorphism with C^n.
quote: A second route uses geometric flow to construct shrinking holomorphic charts and then assembles those charts by complex dynamics.

backbone: Bound mean doubling growth uniformly by a multiscale square-subdivision scheme (affine improvement, descent, persistence, packing; compactness-contradiction lemmas via subharmonic profiles), then transfer to nodal length by Roy-Fortin.

quote: Section~\ref{sel:section} estimates the selected signed force, and Section~\ref{sec:closure} closes the bootstrap.

backbone: Reduce to finite targets; move Laguerre-cell sites along an optimal coupling at fixed masses, bound map variation by a uniform cell-moment inequality; sharpness via an explicit three-atom example.
